issue: LC-MS isomer concern: 2-phosphoglycerate (C00631) is isobaric; not listed as a separate feature
review_rationale: 3-PG is the dominant phosphoglycerate pool and Li et al. assigned the feature with a 3-PG standard. 2-PG is isobaric and may co-elute, but PGAM1 (interconverts 3-PG and 2-PG) is already in the gene set, so the set covers the sum of both species.

issue: LC-MS isomer concern: glycerol 2-phosphate (C02979) is isobaric; name implies the alpha (1/3) form
review_rationale: 'alpha' names the 1/3 isomer; glycerol 2-phosphate is a minor cellular species. Mapped to sn-glycerol 3-phosphate (MAM02914).

issue: enantiomer present in Human-GEM (MAM01716); LC-MS does not resolve enantiomers
review_rationale: Enantiomer rule (D31). D-lactate (methylglyoxal pathway) is typically <1% of cellular lactate. Mapped to L-lactate (MAM02403); D-lactate (MAM01716) reactions not added.

issue: LC-MS isomer concern: isobaric with other disaccharides (e.g. sucrose listed separately)
review_rationale: Lactose is synthesised only by lactating mammary epithelium (LALBA/B4GALT1); an intracellular signal in cancer lines more plausibly reflects FBS carry-over or an unresolved isobaric disaccharide. A first-neighbour gene set for lactose is not biologically meaningful here.

issue: Human-GEM also contains alpha-NAD(+) (MAM20063), an anomer of NAD+ (MAM02552)
review_rationale: Not decided: fails rule 3 (227 expressed genes) regardless. alpha-NAD+ (MAM20063) is a minor anomer.

issue: LC-MS isomer concern: isobaric with other hexitols (mannitol, galactitol)
review_rationale: Sorbitol (AKR1B1/SORD polyol pathway) is the hexitol human cells make; mannitol is not synthesised by human cells. Caveat: the 12 primary lines in Leibovitz L-15 are grown on galactose, where galactitol (AKR1B1 product, isobaric) is possible.

issue: LC-MS isomer concern: LC-MS does not resolve R/S; isobaric with 3-hydroxybutyrate (separation not documented)
review_rationale: Not decided: fails rule 4 (37% missing) regardless.

issue: enantiomer present in Human-GEM (MAM01638); LC-MS does not resolve enantiomers
review_rationale: Enantiomer rule (D31): LC-MS does not resolve L/D; D-amino acids are trace in cultured human cancer cells. Mapped to the L-form (MAM01307); D-alanine (MAM01638) reactions are not added to the gene set.

issue: LC-MS isomer concern: can form in-source/ex vivo by cyclisation of glutamine/glutamate
review_rationale: 5-oxoproline forms non-enzymatically and in the ion source by cyclisation of glutamine and glutamate, so the measured signal is partly an artefact of much larger pools.
